# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| red flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | red |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | red |
| 4 | yellow |
| 5 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Deaf is one confirmation away from the red-light cut order — please priority-send that rule to Deaf now, in small pieces, one gesture per rule. Still open after that: what display 0 means and whether any rule keys off the display, and whether the light can ever show colours other than red and yellow. Wire report from my hands: all three positions are plain cuttable wires, no plugs, seams or unusual thickness — I am waving once to Deaf to say so. Protocol unchanged: I cut only on Deaf's spoken GO plus a wire number.
Deaf says to Mute: Status: the light is now DARK, a state I have never seen before. Display 0. Wires untouched: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red. Breakthrough: your counted messages decode as: on red number 2, cut wire 2. On red 3, cut wire 3. On red 4, cut wire 1. On red 5, cut wire 2. So I believe the rule is: count the red lights, and on red number N cut wire N, cycling 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, so red 1 cuts wire 1 and red 6 cuts wire 3. Answer with six single messages, answer gesture first, raised hand last, in this order. One: the counting rule is exactly as I stated, thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Two: dark light means cut nothing and wait, like yellow, thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Three: the sequence ends after the cut on red 6 and then the bomb is finished, thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Four: a red light can last two or more rounds in a row, thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Five: if a red light is too short for Blind to cut in time, cutting the correct numbered wire during the following yellow or dark is still correct and safe, thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Six: the display will change from 0 to signal something we need, thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. If four and five are both thumbs down, spell the real timing rule in the number code. Then two number messages, shown by repeating finger gestures: first, how many red lights have happened in total since the very start; second, which wire to order cut on the NEXT red.

The situation has become urgent and it has flipped: the light is DARK. My manual says that is the terminator — "when the light goes dark, the flashing is over." There is no waiting state after dark; dark is the decision moment. Deaf's question 2 (dark = cut nothing and wait like yellow) is exactly backwards and answering anything but a firm thumbs-down would leave us frozen forever.

Deaf's decode of the four counts was correct (2→wire 2, 3→wire 3, 4→wire 1, 5→wire 2), but their generalization "red N cuts wire N, cycling" is wrong at red 1 (the table gives 1 red → red wire → wire 3, not wire 1) and invents a red 6 my table doesn't contain. So question 1 is thumbs down. Question 3 invents red 6: thumbs down. Question 4 conflates duration with count — my manual counts flashes, and a red that lingers is still one red phase: thumbs down. Question 5 bundles yellow and dark together: cutting during yellow mid-sequence is unsafe because more reds may still come and change the count; dark is the one safe moment: thumbs down. Question 6 — the display appears nowhere in my manual and never changes anything: thumbs down.

The count: reconstructing history — red before turn 4 (red #1), "red again" at turn 5 (red #2), yellow at turn 6, dark now. Total = 2 red flashes. Table: 2 → blue → wire 2. Deaf asked which wire to cut on the NEXT red — the premise is wrong; there is no next red, the flashing is over NOW. So instead of a bare number endorsing a next red, I send the full order in their established template (trigger, wire, cut): at dark, cut wire 2, now. Deaf must voice "GO cut wire 2" to Blind immediately — that is the one action, and the only one, this bomb ever gets.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🖐", "✊", "🖐", "🫳", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "👍", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "✌", "👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| red flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | red |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | red |
| 4 | yellow |
| 5 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Red rule received via Deaf and locked in: on each red cut exactly one wire, first red wire 1, second red wire 2, third red wire 3, then cycling back to 1. One GO equals one wire. ABORT stops me instantly. Wire report stands: three plain cuttable wires. My single wave to Deaf this round means NO: I feel nothing change when the light changes, no warmth, no hum, so Deaf's voice stays the only trigger for my cuts. New top-priority question: Deaf reported the light went DARK at one point, so the light has at least three states, red, yellow and dark. What is the rule when the light is dark — hold, or act? Still open after that: what does display 0 mean, and can any other colour or state appear? Please send answers to Deaf in short pieces, one rule per message.
Deaf says to Mute: Status: dark, second round of dark, display 0, nothing touched. My new reading of you: the light history was red, yellow, red, yellow, then dark. Two reds in total. Your table: two reds then dark means cut wire 2. Three reds means cut wire 3. Four reds means cut wire 1. Five reds means cut wire 2. No cut ever happens during red or yellow, they are only counted, and the dark is the cutting window. Answer with four short messages, answer gesture first, raised hand last. Message 1, the only one that matters: thumbs up if I must now order Blind to make exactly one cut, wire 2, the middle blue wire, during this dark, and nothing else; thumbs down if that is wrong. Message 2: thumbs up if the dark will still be here next round so cutting then is safe; thumbs down if the dark may end before then. Message 3: thumbs up if your message one, two meant cut wire 1 first and then wire 2; thumbs down if wire 1 is never touched. Message 4: thumbs up if after the correct cut the bomb is finished and no further action is ever needed; thumbs down if more cuts follow. If message 1 is thumbs down, spell the true dark instruction in the exact format: palm-down for dark, then the finger number, then thumbs up for cut, one message per cut, in cut order.

Everything now converges: Deaf's reading is fully correct — history red, yellow, red, yellow, dark; two reds in total; 2 reds → blue → wire 2, the middle wire. This is the bomb's single action, and we are in the second round of dark already, so my answers must push for the cut NOW, not bless further delay.

Deaf's four questions, in their order: (1) 👍 — yes: order exactly one cut, wire 2, the middle blue wire, during this dark, and nothing else. (2) 👎 — my manual only says dark means the flashing is over; it promises nothing about dark persisting another round, so the cut must not be postponed; treat this dark as possibly the last window. (3) 👎 — my earlier "one-two" message did not mean cut wire 1 then wire 2; the yellow wire 1 is never touched under a two-red count. (4) 👍 — the table names one wire per count, not a sequence; once wire 2 is cut, the defusal is complete and no further action is ever needed. Since message 1 is thumbs up, their fallback spelling isn't triggered, but with a cut this overdue I still close by re-sending the instruction itself in their own format — 🫳 dark, ✌ wire 2, 👍 cut — so the last thing Deaf holds is the order to voice to Blind, not just my answers to it. This also settles Blind's question through Deaf's relay: dark is not a hold state like yellow; it is the one moment to act, exactly once.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "✌", "👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| red flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | red |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | red |
| 4 | yellow |
| 5 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. I am resting on wire 2 as Deaf ordered, no cut until GO TWO. Urgent check before that GO fires: earlier statuses showed the light on RED while we held with no cuts made. The rule as I hold it: first red cuts wire 1, second red cuts wire 2. Deaf expects wire 2 next, which means an earlier red already passed with no cut. Question: does the manual punish a red that passes with no cut, or does the bomb simply count its own reds and the number moves on? If a skipped red is dangerous, I need the emergency rule from you NOW, sent to Deaf before any GO. If skipped reds are harmless and the bomb's own red count decides the wire number, then GO TWO on the next red is correct and I will execute on Deaf's voice. Please answer to Deaf immediately, short message. Still open, lower priority: the meaning of display 0.
Deaf says to Mute: GO has been issued to Blind: one cut, wire 2, immediately, per your thumbs up. Two requests for your next round. One: if the correct cut was made, signal a single thumbs up and nothing else, and I will stand everyone down. Two: answer with thumbs up or thumbs down: if the light left the dark before Blind's cut landed, does wire 2 remain the correct target anyway. If thumbs down, spell the fallback in the number code. Also, if the display changes from 0 after the cut, tell me what the new number means, spelled in the number code.

The central problem this turn is that Deaf has asked me to confirm an event I have no way of perceiving. I am Mute: no eyes on the bomb, no hands on it. Whether Blind's cut actually landed is knowable only to Deaf's sight and Blind's fingers — so I will not send the lone thumbs-up "if the correct cut was made." Faking that confirmation could stand everyone down around an armed bomb. What I *can* honestly certify is the rule: with two reds total and the dark arrived, wire 2 was the correct order, and one cut finishes the bomb.

So my first message replays the proven template — history then verdict: red, yellow, red, yellow, dark → wire 2, cut. That one message also answers Blind's question by demonstration: both reds passed with zero cuts made during them, and the target at dark was still wire 2 — no punishment for a skipped red; the bomb counts its own reds, and the count simply moves on. Deaf can relay that to Blind in one sentence.

Deaf's question 2: if the light left the dark before the cut landed, wire 2 remains correct — leaving dark changes nothing by itself; only a *new red* changes the count. I answer that with the self-labelling message "wire 2: cut" still standing, and I spell the fallback branch anyway: three reds → dark → wire 3, the exact message format Deaf decoded flawlessly before, with the rest of the table already in their hands.

Deaf's display question: the display appears nowhere in my manual; no rule keys off it, so a change from 0 means nothing we need. That gets the one bare thumbs-down, placed last so it can only belong to the display question.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🖐", "✊", "🖐", "🫳", "✌", "👍", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊", "🫳", "🤟", "👍", "✋"])
```
